image_description: A close-up shot of a person holding a baseball in their right hand. The ball is the central focus, displaying white leather and red stitching with visible text/branding. The background includes parts of the person's body (face, legs in jeans) and dark surroundings.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The object is clearly spherical and fits naturally in the human hand, consistent with standard baseball dimensions.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Perfectly round with uniform surface texture.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The silhouette is circular without obvious flattening or warping. The leather texture appears consistent across the visible surface.
The cover is white/off-white with a texture resembling leather grain.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Cover consists of two figure-eight-shaped pieces stitched together.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The seam pattern follows the characteristic figure-eight geometry typical of baseball construction.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Raised red thread forming distinctive curved seam pattern with numerous double stitches.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Red stitching is clearly visible, raised, and follows the curved seams. Individual stitch marks are discernible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Red stitching provides high contrast against white background.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The red color stands out sharply against the white leather.
There are specular highlights on the ball's surface indicating a smooth, slightly reflective finish.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Firm but slightly compressible feel from cork and rubber core wrapped in yarn.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Internal composition and tactile properties cannot be visually verified.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: White cover with red stitching is traditional appearance.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visual appearance matches the standard aesthetic of a regulation baseball.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The blue/green text printed on the ball is illegible and distorted. While real baseballs have branding, AI often fails to render crisp, readable text, resulting in 'fake' lettering that looks like text but isn't.
The puncture holes for the stitching lack consistent depth and definition; some appear as flat red lines rather than thread passing through leather.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the object is taxonomically classified as a baseball and not a similar spherical object.
To analyze the illegible branding text for signs of AI generation artifacts (gibberish characters).
To verify the boundary between the ball and the hand/background is sharp and free of bleeding/fusion artifacts.
To assess overall lighting consistency and detect subtle structural deformations in the hand holding the ball.

focus_areas: Legibility and structure of printed text on the ball
Geometric integrity of the red stitching pattern
Boundary separation between fingers and the ball surface
Lighting consistency on the spherical surface
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the text on the baseball. Real baseballs have clear branding (e.g., Rawlings, Official League). AI often generates pseudo-text. If the text is gibberish, flag it as an artifact even if the rest of the ball looks good. Also, check if the fingers holding the ball merge into the leather texture.
